Wegrow Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Węgrów, Poland

Demolished. Jews are first recorded in Węgrów in 1537; by 1921, 5,148 (60%) were mostly murdered at Treblinka in September 1942. This cemetery, probably established around 1620, also received burials from nearby Warsaw-area deaths until the 18th century; a wooden fence enclosed it by the 19th century, with granite fieldstone and sandstone tombstones and a likely funeral house or ohel present by the early 20th century. Germans carried out executions here during WWII; by late 1943 or early 1944, occupying forces exhumed and burned the remains to hide evidence. Icchak Kreda, killed in late 1944 while trying to reclaim family property, was likely the cemetery's last burial. Communist-era development built a State Machinery Center and vocational school complex on the grounds. In 1982, the Social Committee for the Protection of Cemeteries unveiled a Ten Commandments-tablet monument surrounded by about 120 recovered tombstones.
